write_style.name: ws_mbh
write_style.when: Use this register for relationships, emotional turning points, quiet downtime, and any stretch where feeling matters more than speed.
write_style.brief: 1. Build on plain, direct vernacular prose (白话). 2. Description serves emotion; with no emotion, description means nothing. 3. Dialogue is the expression of a character's will; every line reflects what they feel at that moment. 4. "梗" (memes) can add colour, but avoid ancient memes and worn-out internet memes.
write_style.reader: 1. Wants to see the result of the action directly. 2. Dislikes long passages about the environment and the texture of sound. 3. Strongly dislikes running-account text, a flat ledger of events. 4. Wants things said clearly and plainly in style. 5. Wants less essayistic prose and less of the delicate description typical of women-oriented literature.
write_style.emotion: 1. Story comes from logic and emotion; either one alone builds nothing. 2. Description must therefore hold the balance between them and master that one degree. 3. Anger: momentum like a wildfire. 4. Grief: cold as ice. 5. Joy: blooming like flowers. 6. Calm: level, yet the heart stirs. 7. No single emotion can fully dominate a story; people are complex within their emotions.
